extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (primary and assistant) and patent prosecution practitioners (applicants/attorneys/agents)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive guidance from the MPEP on when and how examiners should document reasons for allowance, handling of notices of allowance/issue fees, deferral and withdrawal from issue, and related post-allowance practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information Disclosure Statement handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify that each reference on the Information Disclosure Statement has either been initialed by the examiner or lined-through by the examiner. All lists of references are maintained in the application file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must ensure IDS references are properly marked in the file; maintain lists of references in the application file for clear record-keeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make of record references after interference/derivation
rubrics_metrics.description: In the first action after termination of an interference or derivation, the examiner should make of record in each application all references not already of record which were pertinent to any preliminary motions and which were discussed in the decision on motion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure references relied on during preliminary motions and decisions are added promptly to each affected application file so the prosecution record is complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of erroneous citation before issue
rubrics_metrics.description: In any application, otherwise ready for issue, in which an erroneous citation has not been formally corrected in an official paper, the examiner is directed to correct the citation by an examiner’s amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use examiner’s amendment to correct citations (see MPEP § 707.05(g)); do not allow erroneous citations to remain uncorrected in files ready for issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding new references after application is in issue
rubrics_metrics.description: Any new reference cited when the application is in issue, under the practice of MPEP § 1308.01, should be added by way of a PTO-892 or PTO/SB/08.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedural forms (PTO-892 or PTO/SB/08) when adding references after an application is in issue to ensure proper docketing and record entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signing: E-signatures and Issue Classification Sheet
rubrics_metrics.description: The primary examiner and the assistant examiner involved in the allowance of an application will apply E-Signatures on the Issue Classification sheet. A primary examiner who prepares an application for issue signs the file wrapper only in the 'Primary Examiner' box on the Issue Classification sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only the names on the Issue Classification Sheet will be listed in the printed patent; ensure e-signature procedures and correct signature boxes are used.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to set forth reasons for allowance (37 CFR 1.104(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner believes that the record of the prosecution as a whole does not make clear his or her reasons for allowing a claim or claims, the examiner may set forth such reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons may be in an Office action rejecting other claims or a separate communication; applicant may comment and the examiner’s failure to respond to comments does not imply anything. The purpose is to improve the quality and reliability of issued patents by providing a clear file history.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner responsibility to make file history complete
rubrics_metrics.description: While setting forth reasons for allowance is not mandatory, the examiner should see that the file history is as complete as is reasonably possible, exercising responsibility to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When record does not clearly reflect reasons for allowance, examiner should make specific reasons of record; the guidelines are illustrative not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required content when reasons are recorded (minimum content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each statement should include at least (1) the major difference in the claims not found in the prior art of record, and (2) the reasons why that difference is considered to define patentability over the prior art if either of these reasons for allowance is not clear in the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statements should be accurate, precise, and avoid placing unwarranted interpretations upon claims; avoid stock paragraphs or meaningless boilerplate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid using statements to create unsupported claim narrowing or special definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: It is improper to use a statement of reasons for allowance to attempt to narrow a claim by providing a special definition to a claim limitation which is argued by applicant, but not supported by a special definition in the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not provide or imply special definitions or limitations in the statement that are unsupported by the specification; be mindful of possible misinterpretations and legal effects (e.g., Festo implications).

rubrics_metrics.name: When reasons for allowance are unnecessary (record sufficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, the examiner’s actions and the applicant’s replies make evident the reasons for allowance, satisfying the 'record as a whole' proviso; in such cases no separate statement should be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particularly true when applicant fully complies with 37 CFR 1.111(b),(c) and 1.133(b); only add statements when clarity is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of situations likely requiring a statement (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative examples of when it is likely a statement should be added to the record are provided (A through I) to aid examiners in judgment under 37 CFR 1.104(e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the enumerated examples as guidance to identify cases where reasons for allowance should be recorded; the list is illustrative not exhaustive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation A: Claims allowed based on one of multiple arguments/affidavits
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims are allowed on the basis of one (or some) of a number of arguments and/or affidavits presented, and a statement is necessary to identify which of these were persuasive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include when arguments are in an appeal brief, ordinary reply (with or without amendment), or where both an affidavit under 37 CFR 1.131 and arguments concerning 102/103 are presented; identify which arguments/affidavits persuaded allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation B: First-action allowance where reasons are not discussed
rubrics_metrics.description: First action allowance: (1) of a noncontinuing application wherein claims are very close to cited prior art and differences not discussed elsewhere; (2) of a continuing application where reasons for allowance are not apparent from the parent case or preliminary filed matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allowance occurs at first action or in a continuing app lacking clear parent-record reasons, include a clear statement of reasons of allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation C: Withdrawal of a rejection for reasons not suggested by applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Withdrawal of a rejection for reasons not suggested by applicant, e.g., as a result of an appeal or pre-appeal brief conference; when applicant’s arguments were misdirected or not persuasive alone and examiner finds a more cogent argument; when claims amended to avoid a 102 rejection but obviousness remains unaddressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record the examiner’s reasoning when withdrawal of a rejection arises from the examiner’s new grounds or reasoning not argued by applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation D: Allowance after remand from the PTAB
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowance after remand from the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When allowance follows remand, the reasons for allowance should be made of record and may need to reference the remand decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation E: Allowance coincident with citation of newly found references
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowance coincident with the citation of newly found references that are very close to the claims, but claims are considered patentable thereover.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record why claims are patentable over newly-cited references, whether the reference was filed/cited by applicant or found/cited by examiner, even if not argued.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation F: Reasons are on record but unclear/spread throughout file
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the reasons for allowance are of record but, in the examiner’s judgment, are unclear (e.g., spread throughout the file history) so that an unreasonable effort would be required to collect them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consolidate and state principal reasons to make the file history clear rather than requiring others to piece together disparate file entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation G: Allowance based on non-obvious claim interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowance based on a claim interpretation which might not be readily apparent, for example: (1) article claims in which method limitations impart patentability; (2) method claims in which article limitations impart patentability; (3) claim drafted so that 'nonanalogous' art is not applicable; (4) preamble or functional language 'breathes life' into claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain the interpretive basis (e.g., interplay of claim types, functional language, nonanalogous art) underlying allowance so the rationale is evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation H: Allowance following court decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Allowance following decision by the United States Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or District Court of the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reasons for allowance should refer to and incorporate the briefs and the court decision where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Situation I: Allowance based on PCT search report references
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the claims are considered patentable over the X and/or Y references cited in a search report of a corresponding PCT application and the reasons for allowance are not apparent from the record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on PCT search report references, state why the claims are patentable over those cited X/Y references when the record does not already make this clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of suitable statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: Illustrative acceptable statements (examples A–G) show the form suitable for reasons for allowance: identify specific claim limitations (e.g., 'inclusion of .03 to .05 percent nickel'), reference applicant affidavits showing unexpected results, reference telephonic interview substance and agreed amendments, compare to specific prior patents, incorporate court decisions, identify agreed claim limitations from interviews or amendments, explain non-obviousness reasoning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use concrete, specific factual and legal bases (limitations, dates, interviews, affidavits, court decisions) rather than vague assertions; provide enough detail to show why the claims are patentable without overclaiming completeness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples of unsuitable statement content
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements not suitable include vague technical descriptions without explanation of significance, statements that merely recite that applicant’s remarks or agreements occurred without explaining why persuasive, broad assertions that no prior art corresponds without support, or generic statements 'Claims 1-6 have been allowed because they are believed to be both novel and nonobvious.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include matter that does not relate directly to reasons for allowance; avoid statements that fail to make clear the examiner’s substantive basis for allowance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for placing statement of reasons in the file
rubrics_metrics.description: Most instances when examiner finds need to place a statement of reasons will come at time of allowance. Examiner should (a) check appropriate box on PTOL-37 and (b) attach a paper containing the examiner's statement of reasons for allowance, clearly labeled and identifying the application number. The paper should specify that comments may be filed by the applicant and preferably be submitted with payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 13.03 may be used; the paper should be labeled 'Statement of Reasons for Allowance.' For pre-allowance communications use form paragraph 13.03.01. Do not use form paragraph 13.03 in reexamination (see form paragraph 22.16).

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant comments on examiner’s statement of reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file comments on the examiner’s statement of reasons for allowance, preferably no later than payment of the issue fee. Such comments will be entered in the application file and labeled 'Comments on Statement of Reasons for Allowance.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner’s statement is the examiner’s personal opinion and should not create estoppel; only applicant’s statements create estoppel. Failure to comment should not be treated as acquiescence. Examiner may review and comment on applicant's submission but has no obligation to do so.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Allowance: timing and fee payment (37 CFR 1.311)
rubrics_metrics.description: If, on examination, it appears that the applicant is entitled to a patent, a notice of allowance will be sent to the applicant. The notice shall specify a sum constituting the issue fee and any required publication fee which must both be paid within three months from the date of mailing of the notice of allowance to avoid abandonment. This three-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PTOL-85 (Notice of Allowance and Fee(s) Due) is mailed; Part B (PTOL-85B) must be returned with payment. Use fee transmittal PTOL-85B; the fee amounts are shown on the Notice. The Office will record the mailing date in the image file wrapper table of contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit account authorization and fee transmittal practices
rubrics_metrics.description: An authorization to charge the issue fee to a deposit account may be filed only after mailing of the notice of allowance. Submission of an incorrect issue fee or a fee transmittal form without payment will operate as a request to charge the correct issue fee to a deposit account if authorized.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are urged to use PTOL-85B when submitting payments. If deposit account info is added but the check box authorizing charge is not checked, the deposit account will still be charged the required fees. Fee(s) may be accepted from applicant, assignee, or registered attorney/agent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Issue fee amounts, entity discounts, and credits
rubrics_metrics.description: Under PLTIA changes the sum specified in the Notice of Allowance constitutes the issue fee and any required publication fee; amounts due under 35 U.S.C. 41(a) are reduced by 60% for small entities and 80% for micro entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice of Allowance reflects issue fee amount due and any previously paid issue fee; return of PTOL-85B can request reapplication of a previously paid issue fee toward a new due amount (e.g., after RCE).

rubrics_metrics.name: No extension or Director authority to extend issue fee time
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director has no authority to extend the time for paying the issue fee. Intentional failure to pay the issue fee within the 3 months permitted does not amount to unintentional delay in making payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the three-month period as firm; plan filings/payments to avoid abandonment due to missed non-extendable deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oath/declaration requirement prior to allowance (post-Sept 16, 2012 apps)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed on or after Sept 16, 2012, if an application is in condition for allowance but does not include an oath or declaration in compliance with 37 CFR 1.63, or a substitute statement in compliance with 37 CFR 1.64, the Office will issue a Notice of Allowability (PTOL-37) including a Notice Requiring Inventor’s Oath or Declaration (PTOL-2306) requiring the filing of the oath/declaration no later than the date of payment of the issue fee to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to file a proper oath/declaration before or with payment of the issue fee, the application will be regarded as abandoned (see 37 CFR 1.53(f)(3)(ii)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deferring issuance of a patent (37 CFR 1.314)
rubrics_metrics.description: To request that the Office defer issuance of a patent, applicant must file a petition under 37 CFR 1.314 including the fee and a showing of good and sufficient reasons why it is necessary to defer issuance of the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO policy is generally to defer issuance for up to 1 month only absent extraordinary circumstances. Negotiation of licenses, foreign filing timing, collecting data for CIP, or desire for simultaneous issuance are not ordinarily 'extraordinary.' Petition not appropriate until issue fee is paid; petition not effective if not granted prior to issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simultaneous issuance of patents: requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Simultaneous issuance will be granted only when each allowed application has reached the stage of having a mailed PTOL-85; the request must contain for each allowed application: application number, filing date, inventor names, title, and date of allowance. Separate copies of the request must accompany each PTOL-85B.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generally not granted unless all applications have reached the same processing stage; send requests to Mail Stop Issue Fee with required data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practice after payment of issue fee and Issue Notification monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Patents issue shortly after payment of the issue fee; applicants have limited time after payment to file continuing applications, QPIDS, or petitions to withdraw. Best practice is to file such submissions before payment of the issue fee. Applications should be monitored for assignment of patent number and issue date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO issues and publishes grants electronically (Patent Center); applicants participating in e-Office action program get email notification of Issue Notification; avoid filing unnecessary papers after Notice of Allowance; duplicate filings are discouraged and may be treated as failure to engage in reasonable efforts to conclude prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments received after allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: If the amendment is filed under 37 CFR 1.312, follow MPEP § 714.15–714.16(e). If the amendment contains claims copied from a patent to provoke an interference, see MPEP Chapter 2300. Replacement drawings filed after allowance should be forwarded to the Office of Data Management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any paper filed after receiving the Issue Notification should include the indicated patent number, unless the application has been withdrawn from issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of 'Secrecy Order' and D-10 notice
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 'Secrecy Order' in an application is withdrawn after the D-10 notice is mailed, the application should then be treated like an ordinary application in condition for allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy Order apps are not sent to issue even when claims allowed; instead of Notice of Allowance, a D-10 Notice is sent (see MPEP § 130).

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue: general petition rule (37 CFR 1.313)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be withdrawn from issue for further action at the initiative of the Office or upon petition by the applicant. To request withdrawal, applicant must file a petition including the fee and a showing of good and sufficient reasons. A petition is not required if an RCE is filed prior to payment of the issue fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Office withdraws the application from issue, a new Notice of Allowance will be issued if the Office again allows the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue after payment of the issue fee — Office-initiated grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the issue fee has been paid, the Office will not withdraw the application from issue at its own initiative for any reason except: (1) a mistake on the part of the Office; (2) a violation of § 1.56 or illegality in the application; (3) unpatentability of one or more claims; or (4) for interference or derivation proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office-initiated withdrawal after fee payment is limited to these enumerated circumstances; withdrawal will result in issuance of a new Notice of Allowance if again allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal from issue after payment of the issue fee — applicant-initiated grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the issue fee has been paid, the application will not be withdrawn from issue upon petition by the applicant for any reason except: (1) unpatentability of one or more claims accompanied by an unequivocal statement that one or more claims are unpatentable, an amendment to such claim(s), and explanation how amendment causes patentability; (2) consideration of a request for continued examination (RCE) in compliance with § 1.114; or (3) express abandonment of the application (may be in favor of a continuing application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition must be actually received and granted before the date of issue to be effective; withdrawal after payment may not avoid publication of application information.
